intro: Beside a lake in Bursa province lies Nicaea, an ancient city whose story begins in the 4th century BC. Its 5 km of walls still stand, and this is the city that hosted the church councils.
history: The city was founded by Antigonus, one of Alexander's generals. In AD 325 it hosted the Council of Nicaea, and later it served as a Byzantine capital.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Roman walls and the Istanbul Gate. Visit the theatre and the Hagia Sophia (Orhan Mosque), and look for the lake basilica.
facts: Did you know? A 4th-century basilica lies submerged beneath the waters of Lake İznik. The Council of Nicaea met here in 325 and wrote the creed still recited today. In 787 the city hosted a second council, which brought iconoclasm to an end. And when the crusaders took Constantinople in 1204, Nicaea became the Byzantine capital in exile; it was from here that the empire was won back.
outro: This brings our journey through Nicaea to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
